literature.headline_zh: 麻疹病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期麻疹病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 来自接种疫苗的个体的 麻疹 传播 虽然相对不常见,但可能有助于 暴发。荟萃分析发现,消灭地区接种疫苗的传播者比非消灭地区的传播者年龄更大,91%的研究提供了后续传播世代的数据,每个接种疫苗的传播者中位数为4例。 [10.1080/14760584.2026.2708188]
与较轻的病例相比,重症 COVID-19 和严重胸部 CT 受累的患者中观察到较高的抗 麻疹 IgG 滴度。调整后,抗 麻疹 IgG 滴度仍与严重胸部 CT 受累独立相关,但与 死亡率 或 ICU 入住不独立相关。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10512804/v1]
麻疹病毒 H 蛋白中未检测到 SNP,但 F 蛋白中 30.0-40.9% 的 基因组 中存在非同义多态性;风疹衣壳C和E2糖蛋白中的SNP发生率高达30%,而腮腺炎HN和F抗原中的SNP发生率低于20%。 [10.30895/2221-996x-2026-750]
结果表明,尽管 疫苗接种 覆盖率和有效率较高,但零星或小规模的 麻疹 暴发 仍然存在。 [10.1142/s1793524526500749]
根据世界卫生组织 (WHO) [1] 的数据,自 COVID-19 大流行以来,全球 麻疹 病例数量稳步增加(表 1)。 [10.1080/21505594.2026.2713277]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Measles transmissions from vaccinated individuals, although relatively uncommon, can contribute to outbreaks. [10.1080/14760584.2026.2708188]
Higher anti-measles IgG titers were observed in patients with severe COVID-19 and severe thoracic CT involvement compared with milder cases. [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10512804/v1]

No SNPs were detected in the measles virus H protein, but a nonsynonymous polymorphism in the F protein was present in 30.0–40.9% of genomes; SNPs in rubella capsid C and E2 glycoprotein occurred up to 30%, and in mumps HN and F antigens occurred in less than 20%. [10.30895/2221-996x-2026-750]
The results indicate that sporadic or small-scale measles outbreaks still occur despite high vaccination coverage and efficacy rates. [10.1142/s1793524526500749]
According to the World Health Organization (WHO) [1], the number of global measles cases has steadily increased since the COVID-19 pandemic (Table 1). [10.1080/21505594.2026.2713277]

news.headline_zh: 麻疹病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期麻疹病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 据报道,麻疹 暴发 正在增长;大多数病例发生在未接种疫苗的人身上。该报告是一篇引用当地公共卫生信息的媒体文章。 [news-b6325876d083280b]
CIDRAP 报告称,美国 麻疹 病例总数已超过 2,500 例,新增 101 例。 [news-2e98fcf42ba41322]
俄亥俄州 2026 年第三次 麻疹 麻疹,由地方和州卫生部门报告;确诊病例数上升并超过 2025 年总数;俄亥俄州卫生部 (ODH) 和县卫生部门正在调查并报告暴露情况。 [news-2aec51b74d3b2e14]
症状在接触后 7-14 天出现,可能导致严重并发症,包括肺炎、脑炎(脑部炎症)、腹泻或死亡,特别是对于未接种疫苗的人。 [news-f42331714ed72e2e]
威斯康星州在爱荷华州和拉斐特县确认了两例新的 麻疹 病例,并警告称可能会出现更多传播。 [news-ca65a9956295d185]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Measles virus news developments.
key_findings_en: A measles outbreak is reported as growing; most cases occurred in people who were not vaccinated. The report is a media article citing local public-health information. [news-b6325876d083280b]
CIDRAP reported that the US measles total has surpassed 2,500 cases, with 101 new cases recorded. [news-2e98fcf42ba41322]

Third measles outbreak of 2026 in Ohio, reported by local and state health departments; confirmed cases rising and surpassing 2025 totals; Ohio Department of Health (ODH) and county health departments are investigating and reporting exposures. [news-2aec51b74d3b2e14]

Symptoms appear 7–14 days after exposure and can lead to severe complications, including pneumonia , encephalitis ( brain inflammation ), diarrhea , or death, particularly in people who are unvaccinated. [news-f42331714ed72e2e]
Wisconsin confirms two new measles cases in Iowa and Lafayette counties, with a warning of more spread. [news-ca65a9956295d185]

papers.title: Do vaccinated cases transmit measles? A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We reviewed evidence on whether vaccinated individuals can transmit measles and conducted a meta-analysis to understand transmission characteristics. METHODS: We searched and extracted data from peer-reviewed and gray literature and included studies reporting measles transmission events from vaccinated individuals. We meta-analyzed the data to calculate the median number of transmissions from vaccinated cases by measles burden, number of doses, and time since first and last dose. RESULTS: We identified 11,911 peer-reviewed and 22 gray literature records and included 33 articles in our review. Seventy individuals who had received 1 or more doses of measles-containing vaccine transmitted measles virus, resulting in 237 secondary cases. Vaccinated transmitters in eliminated areas were older (median age of 19 years (IQR: 3, 21)) than those in non-eliminated areas (median age 16 years; IQR 13, 18) (p = 0.12). Additionally, 91% (30/33) of studies provided data on subsequent transmission generations, leading to 812 measles cases traced back to vaccinated individuals, with a median of 4 (IQR: 1, 10) cases per vaccinated transmitter. CONCLUSION: Measles transmissions from vaccinated cases, although relatively uncommon, must be considered in public health investigations, as such transmissions can contribute to outbreaks.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on whether vaccinated individuals can transmit measles virus and examines the characteristics of such transmission, including measles burden, number of doses, and time since vaccination. The central question is whether measles transmission occurs from vaccinated individuals and its implications for public health.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic search of peer-reviewed and gray literature, identifying 11,911 records and including 33 articles. The meta-analysis calculated the median number of transmissions from vaccinated cases based on measles burden, number of doses, and time since vaccination.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Measles transmissions from vaccinated individuals, although relatively uncommon, can contribute to outbreaks. The meta-analysis found that vaccinated transmitters in eliminated areas were older than those in non-eliminated areas, and 91% of studies provided data on subsequent transmission generations, with a median of 4 cases per vaccinated transmitter.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the evidence is limited in some areas, particularly regarding the age distribution of vaccinated transmitters and the mechanisms of transmission. There is also a need for more detailed studies on the role of vaccinated individuals in outbreaks.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Public health investigations should consider measles transmissions from vaccinated individuals, especially in areas where measles has been eliminated. Further research is needed to understand the dynamics of transmission from vaccinated cases and to improve outbreak response strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigate whether vaccinated individuals can transmit measles virus. The review included 33 articles from 11,911 peer-reviewed and 22 gray literature records. The meta-analysis found that vaccinated individuals can transmit measles, with a median of 4 secondary cases per vaccinated transmitter. Transmissions from vaccinated cases in eliminated areas were associated with older individuals compared to those in non-eliminated areas. The findings highlight the need to consider vaccinated transmitters in public health investigations and suggest areas for further research to better understand their role in outbreaks.

papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: We reviewed evidence on whether vaccinated individuals can transmit measles and conducted a meta-analysis to understand transmission characteristics. METHODS: We searched and extracted data from peer-reviewed and gray literature and included studies reporting measles transmission events from vaccinated individuals. We meta-analyzed the data to calculate the median number of transmissions from vaccinated cases by measles burden, number of doses, and time since first and last dose. RESULTS: We identified 11,911 peer-reviewed and 22 gray literature records and included 33 articles in our review. Seventy individuals who had received 1 or more doses of measles-containing vaccine transmitted measles virus, resulting in 237 secondary cases. Vaccinated transmitters in eliminated areas were older (median age of 19 years (IQR: 3, 21)) than those in non-eliminated areas (median age 16 years; IQR 13, 18) (p = 0.12). Additionally, 91% (30/33) of studies provided data on subsequent transmission generations, leading to 812 measles cases traced back to vaccinated individuals, with a median of 4 (IQR: 1, 10) cases per vaccinated transmitter. CONCLUSION: Measles transmissions from vaccinated cases, although relatively uncommon, must be considered in public health investigations, as such transmissions can contribute to outbreaks.

papers.title: Operational drivers of measles outbreaks in Uganda: a multi-district outbreak causality analysis, July 2025– March 2026
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Measles outbreaks in Uganda persist despite the availability of an effective vaccine, suggesting persistent immunity gaps and health system weaknesses. We conducted a multi-district outbreak causality analysis (OCA) to identify programmatic and health-system contributors to measles outbreaks and inform measles elimination programming. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods OCA across 12 affected districts in Uganda (2025–2026), guided by the World Health Organization framework. We reviewed measles case investigation reports and triangulated findings with qualitative interviews with district health teams, health workers, surveillance and immunisation staff, community leaders, Village Health Teams, and caregivers. We deductively analysed data to identify causal pathways and contributing factors. Findings were organized into four prespecified analytical themes: immunization service delivery, caregiver access and demand, surveillance and case detection, and outbreak preparedness and response. Results The 12 districts reported 1,302 cases, including 80 laboratory-confirmed cases and 10 suspected deaths (case-fatality rate: 0.77%); 46.5% (n=606) occurred among children aged 18– 59 months. Most cases (65.3%) occurred in unvaccinated children, versus 1.0% in children with both measles-rubella (MR) doses. Across districts, incomplete MR2 implementation, irregular outreach, inconsistent fixed-site vaccination, weak follow-up of children who missed vaccination, and transport and distance barriers contributed to persistent immunity gaps. Low clinical suspicion, limited engagement of Village Health Teams, laboratory and surveillance-information bottlenecks, absence of pre-positioned response plans, delayed response activation, and inadequate isolation capacity further limited early detection and control. Conclusion Measles outbreaks were driven primarily by missed vaccination, especially incomplete delivery of the two-dose MR schedule, compounded by access barriers, delayed case detection, and limited outbreak preparedness. Strengthening routine MR1 and MR2 delivery, targeted catch-up vaccination, community-linked surveillance, and pre-positioned district response plans with clear activation triggers will be critical to closing immunity gaps and accelerating measles elimination in Uganda.

The study highlights that measles outbreaks persist due to missed vaccinations, particularly incomplete delivery of the two-dose measles-rubella (MR) schedule, alongside access barriers, delayed case detection, and limited outbreak preparedness. The evidence base includes case investigation reports and qualitative interviews with district health teams, health workers, and community leaders. To address these issues, the authors recommend strengthening routine MR vaccination, implementing targeted catch-up campaigns, enhancing community-linked surveillance, and establishing pre-positioned response plans with clear activation triggers. These measures are critical for closing immunity gaps and advancing measles elimination efforts in Uganda.

papers.title_zh: 乌干达 麻疹 暴发 的运营驱动因素:多区 暴发 因果关系分析,2025 年 7 月至 2026 年 3 月
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Measles outbreaks in Uganda persist despite the availability of an effective vaccine, suggesting persistent immunity gaps and health system weaknesses. We conducted a multi-district outbreak causality analysis (OCA) to identify programmatic and health-system contributors to measles outbreaks and inform measles elimination programming. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods OCA across 12 affected districts in Uganda (2025–2026), guided by the World Health Organization framework. We reviewed measles case investigation reports and triangulated findings with qualitative interviews with district health teams, health workers, surveillance and immunisation staff, community leaders, Village Health Teams, and caregivers. We deductively analysed data to identify causal pathways and contributing factors. Findings were organized into four prespecified analytical themes: immunization service delivery, caregiver access and demand, surveillance and case detection, and outbreak preparedness and response. Results The 12 districts reported 1,302 cases, including 80 laboratory-confirmed cases and 10 suspected deaths (case-fatality rate: 0.77%); 46.5% (n=606) occurred among children aged 18– 59 months. Most cases (65.3%) occurred in unvaccinated children, versus 1.0% in children with both measles-rubella (MR) doses. Across districts, incomplete MR2 implementation, irregular outreach, inconsistent fixed-site vaccination, weak follow-up of children who missed vaccination, and transport and distance barriers contributed to persistent immunity gaps. Low clinical suspicion, limited engagement of Village Health Teams, laboratory and surveillance-information bottlenecks, absence of pre-positioned response plans, delayed response activation, and inadequate isolation capacity further limited early detection and control. Conclusion Measles outbreaks were driven primarily by missed vaccination, especially incomplete delivery of the two-dose MR schedule, compounded by access barriers, delayed case detection, and limited outbreak preparedness. Strengthening routine MR1 and MR2 delivery, targeted catch-up vaccination, community-linked surveillance, and pre-positioned district response plans with clear activation triggers will be critical to closing immunity gaps and accelerating measles elimination in Uganda.

papers.title: Integrated Computational Design and Molecular Dynamics Evaluation of Novel siRNAs Targeting the Hemagglutinin Gene of Measles Virus
papers.abstract: Abstract Despite the availability of an effective vaccine, measles virus (MV) remains a major global health concern because no approved antiviral therapeutics currently exist. RNA interference (RNAi) is a promising antiviral strategy, but studies targeting the conserved MV hemagglutinin (H) gene are limited. In this study, an integrated computational pipeline was used to identify and evaluate novel siRNA candidates targeting the MV H gene. At first, 96 MV strains were used to perform multiple sequence alignment (MSA) to generate a consensus sequence, and the phylogenetic tree demonstrated limited genetic divergence among the strains. 11 siRNA candidates were then designed and screened for off-target effects. Subsequently, they were subjected to thermodynamic analysis, secondary and tertiary structure prediction, hybridization energy evaluation, and molecular docking against human Argonaute-2 (hAgo2). The docking results showed that S3, S4, and S7 displayed docking scores of -367.22, − 349.03, and − 383.07 kcal/mol with the most favorable binding orientation within the catalytic PIWI domain of hAgo2. The three selected candidates maintained stable structural behavior throughout 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. These computational analyses indicate that the S3, S4, and S7 may serve as promising siRNA candidates against the MV H gene, which require further in vitro gene silencing assays and in vivo validation.

In this study, an integrated computational pipeline was used to identify and evaluate novel siRNA candidates targeting the MV H gene. At first, 96 MV strains were used to perform multiple sequence alignment (MSA) to generate a consensus sequence, and the phylogenetic tree demonstrated limited genetic divergence among the strains. 11 siRNA candidates were then designed and screened for off-target effects. Subsequently, they were subjected to thermodynamic analysis, secondary and tertiary structure prediction, hybridization energy evaluation, and molecular docking against human Argonaute-2 (hAgo2). The docking results showed that S3, S4, and S7 displayed docking scores of -367.22, − 349.03, and − 383.07 kcal/mol with the most favorable binding orientation within the catalytic PIWI domain of hAgo2. The three selected candidates maintained stable structural behavior throughout 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. These computational analyses indicate that the S3, S4, and S7 may serve as promising siRNA candidates against the MV H gene, which require further in vitro gene silencing assays and in vivo validation.

analysis.summary_en: This computational study aimed to address the lack of approved antiviral therapeutics for measles virus (MV) by designing and evaluating siRNA candidates targeting the conserved hemagglutinin (H) gene. Using 96 MV strains, the authors performed multiple sequence alignment and phylogenetic analysis to identify conserved regions, followed by the design of 11 siRNA candidates. These candidates underwent thermodynamic analysis, structural prediction, docking against human Argonaute-2, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations. The top three candidates (S3, S4, S7) demonstrated favorable docking scores and stable structural behavior, suggesting potential as antiviral agents. However, the study is limited to computational predictions without experimental validation, and the evidence strength is low, requiring in vitro and in vivo studies to confirm efficacy and safety.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要:尽管存在有效的 疫苗,但 麻疹病毒 (MV) 仍然是全球主要的健康问题,因为目前尚无批准的 抗病毒药物 疗法。RNA 干扰 (RNAi) 是一种很有前景的 抗病毒药物 策略,但针对保守的 MV 血凝素 (H) 基因的研究有限。在本研究中,使用集成计算流程来识别和评估针对 MV H 基因的新型 siRNA 候选物。首先,使用96个MV毒株进行多重序列比对(MSA)以生成共有序列,系统发育树显示毒株之间的遗传差异有限。然后设计并筛选 11 种 siRNA 候选物的脱靶效应。随后,对它们进行了热力学分析、二级和三级结构预测、杂交能量评估以及与人类Argonaute-2(hAgo2)的分子对接。对接结果显示,S3、S4和S7的对接分数分别为-367.22、- 349.03和- 383.07 kcal/mol,在hAgo2的催化PIWI结构域内具有最有利的结合方向。选定的三个候选者在 100 ns 分子动力学 (MD) 模拟过程中保持稳定的结构行为。这些计算分析表明,S3、S4 和 S7 可能作为针对 MV H 基因的有希望的 siRNA 候选物,这需要进一步的体外基因沉默测定和体内验证。

papers.title: Otimização da logística laboratorial e monitoramento de amostras de sangue para diagnóstico do sarampo no Tocantins Optimization of laboratory logistics and blood sample monitoring for measles diagnosis in Tocantins Optimización de la logística de laboratorio y monitoreo de muestras de sangre para diagnóstico de sarampión en Tocantins
papers.abstract: Efficient laboratory logistics is a decisive factor for the quality of health surveillance, especially in territorially extensive settings with structural limitations, such as the state of Tocantins, Brazil. This article analyzes a proposal to optimize the logistics network and monitoring of blood samples intended for measles diagnosis within the Central Public Health Laboratory of Tocantins. The study was based on an institutional diagnosis that identified transport delays, lack of standardized packaging procedures, sample degradation due to failures in the cold chain, lack of traceability, and high costs associated with individualized transportation. Methodologically, this is an applied, qualitative, and descriptive study grounded in institutional empirical data, bibliographic review, and technical-propositional formulation. The results indicate that adopting an integrated logistics model, with regional hubs, route reorganization, operational protocols, and performance indicators, may reduce losses, improve sample reliability, lower operational costs, and strengthen intergovernmental governance between the state and municipalities. The article concludes that logistics rationalization combined with continuous monitoring is a relevant instrument for improving public expenditure quality and strengthening the epidemiological response within Brazil’s Unified Health System.

The study was based on an institutional diagnosis that identified transport delays, lack of standardized packaging procedures, sample degradation due to failures in the cold chain, lack of traceability, and high costs associated with individualized transportation. Methodologically, this is an applied, qualitative, and descriptive study grounded in institutional empirical data, bibliographic review, and technical-propositional formulation. The results indicate that adopting an integrated logistics model, with regional hubs, route reorganization, operational protocols, and performance indicators, may reduce losses, improve sample reliability, lower operational costs, and strengthen intergovernmental governance between the state and municipalities. The article concludes that logistics rationalization combined with continuous monitoring is a relevant instrument for improving public expenditure quality and strengthening the epidemiological response within Brazil’s Unified Health System.

papers.title: Genetic characterization of production strains of measles, rubella, and mumps viruses by high-throughput sequencing
papers.abstract: Spontaneous mutations often arise and accumulate in the genome of RNA-containing viruses, for example measles, rubella and mumps. Modern requirements for the production of vaccine products containing live vaccine viruses suggest control of the genetic stability of production strains. The method of high throughput sequencing allows to determine all mutations arisen in viral population, and to assess genetic stability of production strains. Analysis of nucleotide sequence of the genomes of seed and production strains of measles (Leningrad-16), rubella (RA27/3) and mumps (Leningrad-3) viruses, in comparison with the reference nucleotide sequences of vaccine strains genomes (submitted in the Gen-Bank database). MATERIALS AND METHODS. Production strains of vaccines (measles culture live, rubella culture live and mumps culture live) were used in this study. Whole genome sequencing was performed using the MGI DNBSEQ G-400 and Illumina NextSeq2000 genetic analyzers. When processing and analyzing the sequencing data, the following programs and tools were used: FastQC v.0.12.1, FastP v.0.23.4, BWA-MEM2 v.2.2.1, VizCoV tool. Analysis of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within the viral population in the studied samples revealed a number of minor variants that, and after further accumulation, may lead to changes in the consensus sequences of the vaccine strains proteins. For the studied measles virus samples, no SNPs were found in the main measles virus antigen H protein, however, a nonsynonymous polymorphism was detected in the F protein, occurring in 30.0–40.9% of the viral genomes. SNPs were found in the capsid protein C and in the surface glycoprotein E2 rubella virus, occurring in the viral population with a frequency of up to 30%. SNPs were found in surface antigens hemagglutinin neuraminidase HN and fusion protein F of mumps virus, occurring in the genomes of less than 20% of viral population. Mutations in the genomes of production strains that could affect the immunogenicity of measles, rubella, and mumps vaccines were not detected. The identified set of minor variants with a frequency of occurrence in viral population of more than 10%, which, with further accumulation, can lead to changes in the consensus sequences of vaccine strains, makes the monitoring of vaccine strains stability using high-throughput sequencing relevant.

papers.title_original: Genetic characterization of production strains of measles, rubella, and mumps viruses by high-throughput sequencing

analysis.research_question_and_background: RNA viruses such as measles virus can accumulate spontaneous mutations that may compromise vaccine strain stability and efficacy, creating a need for genetic monitoring of production strains.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized seed and production strains of measles (Leningrad-16), rubella (RA27/3), and mumps (Leningrad-3) viruses using high-throughput sequencing to assess genetic stability.
analysis.methods: Whole genome sequencing was performed on the MGI DNBSEQ G-400 and Illumina NextSeq2000 platforms, with data processed using FastQC, FastP, BWA-MEM2, and VizCoV tools to identify single nucleotide polymorphisms.
analysis.main_results: No SNPs were detected in the measles virus H protein, but a nonsynonymous polymorphism in the F protein was present in 30.0–40.9% of genomes; SNPs in rubella capsid C and E2 glycoprotein occurred up to 30%, and in mumps HN and F antigens occurred in less than 20%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret minor variant detection as evidence that high-throughput sequencing can monitor vaccine strain stability, highlighting its relevance for early detection of potential immunogenicity-altering mutations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support routine genomic surveillance of measles, rubella, and mumps vaccine production strains to ensure genetic stability and maintain vaccine immunogenicity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not evaluate functional effects of detected polymorphisms on vaccine immunogenicity, limiting causal inference; evidence strength is moderate given the absence of functional assays.

analysis.summary_en: This study used high-throughput sequencing to genetically characterize measles, rubella, and mumps vaccine production strains, comparing seed and production genomes to reference sequences. No mutations were found in the measles H protein, but a nonsynonymous F protein polymorphism occurred in 30–40% of genomes. Rubella and mumps strains showed minor variants in capsid and surface glycoproteins at frequencies up to 30% and less than 20%, respectively. papers.title_zh: 通过高通量测序对 麻疹、风疹和腮腺炎病毒生产株进行遗传表征
papers.source_body_en: Spontaneous mutations often arise and accumulate in the genome of RNA-containing viruses, for example measles, rubella and mumps. Modern requirements for the production of vaccine products containing live vaccine viruses suggest control of the genetic stability of production strains. The method of high throughput sequencing allows to determine all mutations arisen in viral population, and to assess genetic stability of production strains. Analysis of nucleotide sequence of the genomes of seed and production strains of measles (Leningrad-16), rubella (RA27/3) and mumps (Leningrad-3) viruses, in comparison with the reference nucleotide sequences of vaccine strains genomes (submitted in the Gen-Bank database). MATERIALS AND METHODS. Production strains of vaccines (measles culture live, rubella culture live and mumps culture live) were used in this study. Whole genome sequencing was performed using the MGI DNBSEQ G-400 and Illumina NextSeq2000 genetic analyzers. When processing and analyzing the sequencing data, the following programs and tools were used: FastQC v.0.12.1, FastP v.0.23.4, BWA-MEM2 v.2.2.1, VizCoV tool. Analysis of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within the viral population in the studied samples revealed a number of minor variants that, and after further accumulation, may lead to changes in the consensus sequences of the vaccine strains proteins. For the studied measles virus samples, no SNPs were found in the main measles virus antigen H protein, however, a nonsynonymous polymorphism was detected in the F protein, occurring in 30.0–40.9% of the viral genomes. SNPs were found in the capsid protein C and in the surface glycoprotein E2 rubella virus, occurring in the viral population with a frequency of up to 30%. SNPs were found in surface antigens hemagglutinin neuraminidase HN and fusion protein F of mumps virus, occurring in the genomes of less than 20% of viral population. Mutations in the genomes of production strains that could affect the immunogenicity of measles, rubella, and mumps vaccines were not detected. The identified set of minor variants with a frequency of occurrence in viral population of more than 10%, which, with further accumulation, can lead to changes in the consensus sequences of vaccine strains, makes the monitoring of vaccine strains stability using high-throughput sequencing relevant.

papers.title: Association of Measles IgG Antibody Titers with Thoracic CT Severity in Hospitalized Patients with COVID-19
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has a broad clinical spectrum ranging from mild respiratory symptoms to severe pneumonia and death. Previous studies have suggested that pre-existing immunity against measles may influence immune responses during SARS-CoV-2 infection; however, the clinical significance of anti-measles IgG titers in COVID-19 remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the association between anti-measles IgG titers, clinical severity, COVID-19 Mortality Rate (CMR) score, intensive care unit (ICU) requirement, and mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Material and Methods This cross-sectional study included 153 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (86 males and 67 females). Disease severity was classified according to the NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines. Anti-measles IgG levels were measured using an indirect ELISA assay. Mortality risk was assessed using the COVID-19 Mortality Rate (CMR) score. Results Higher anti-measles IgG titers were observed in patients with severe COVID-19 and severe thoracic CT involvement compared with patients with milder disease. Anti-measles IgG titers were significantly higher in patients with severe CT involvement compared with those with non-severe involvement and remained independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement after adjustment for clinical and laboratory parameters. However, anti-measles IgG levels were not independently associated with mortality or ICU admission. Non-survivors were older, had longer hospital stays, higher CMR scores, and lower admission SpO2 levels compared with survivors. Similarly, patients requiring ICU admission had higher CMR scores and more severe thoracic CT involvement. Conclusion Higher anti-measles IgG titers were independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. These findings suggest that anti-measles IgG levels may represent a potential immunological marker associated with pulmonary disease severity rather than a direct marker of mortality risk. Further prospective studies with larger populations are needed to clarify the clinical significance of anti-measles IgG responses in COVID-19.

analysis.research_question_and_background: COVID-19 presents with a wide clinical spectrum, yet the influence of pre-existing anti-measles immunity on SARS-CoV-2 disease severity remains uncertain. The study sought to clarify whether anti-measles IgG titers are associated with clinical severity, mortality risk, ICU requirement, or thoracic CT involvement in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study enrolled 153 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (86 males and 67 females) and classified disease severity according to NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines.
analysis.methods: Anti-measles IgG levels were quantified using an indirect ELISA assay, and mortality risk was assessed with the COVID-19 Mortality Rate (CMR) score. Associations were evaluated after adjustment for clinical and laboratory parameters.
analysis.main_results: Higher anti-measles IgG titers were observed in patients with severe COVID-19 and severe thoracic CT involvement compared with milder cases. Anti-measles IgG titers remained independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement after adjustment, but were not independently associated with mortality or ICU admission.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret anti-measles IgG titers as a potential immunological marker linked to pulmonary disease severity rather than mortality risk. This is the first report of an independent association between anti-measles IgG levels and severe thoracic CT involvement in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: If validated, anti-measles IgG titers could inform risk stratification for pulmonary complications in COVID-19, potentially guiding monitoring or therapeutic strategies in hospitalized patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the single-center sample may reduce generalizability. The evidence is assessed as moderate due to these limitations and the absence of prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study of 153 hospitalized COVID-19 patients found that higher anti-measles IgG titers were independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement but not with mortality or ICU admission. Anti-measles IgG levels were measured by ELISA and severity was classified per NIH guidelines. The authors propose anti-measles IgG as a potential marker of pulmonary disease severity rather than mortality risk. The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and single-center setting, warranting prospective validation.

The study sought to clarify whether anti-measles IgG titers are associated with clinical severity, mortality risk, ICU requirement, or thoracic CT involvement in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study enrolled 153 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (86 males and 67 females) and classified disease severity according to NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines.
elements_en.methods: Anti-measles IgG levels were quantified using an indirect ELISA assay, and mortality risk was assessed with the COVID-19 Mortality Rate (CMR) score. Associations were evaluated after adjustment for clinical and laboratory parameters.
elements_en.main_results: Higher anti-measles IgG titers were observed in patients with severe COVID-19 and severe thoracic CT involvement compared with milder cases. Anti-measles IgG titers remained independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement after adjustment, but were not independently associated with mortality or ICU admission.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret anti-measles IgG titers as a potential immunological marker linked to pulmonary disease severity rather than mortality risk. This is the first report of an independent association between anti-measles IgG levels and severe thoracic CT involvement in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: If validated, anti-measles IgG titers could inform risk stratification for pulmonary complications in COVID-19, potentially guiding monitoring or therapeutic strategies in hospitalized patients.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the single-center sample may reduce generalizability. The evidence is assessed as moderate due to these limitations and the absence of prospective validation.

papers.title_zh: 麻疹 IgG 抗体滴度与住院 COVID-19 患者胸部 CT 严重程度的关系
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has a broad clinical spectrum ranging from mild respiratory symptoms to severe pneumonia and death. Previous studies have suggested that pre-existing immunity against measles may influence immune responses during SARS-CoV-2 infection; however, the clinical significance of anti-measles IgG titers in COVID-19 remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the association between anti-measles IgG titers, clinical severity, COVID-19 Mortality Rate (CMR) score, intensive care unit (ICU) requirement, and mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Material and Methods This cross-sectional study included 153 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (86 males and 67 females). Disease severity was classified according to the NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines. Anti-measles IgG levels were measured using an indirect ELISA assay. Mortality risk was assessed using the COVID-19 Mortality Rate (CMR) score. Results Higher anti-measles IgG titers were observed in patients with severe COVID-19 and severe thoracic CT involvement compared with patients with milder disease. Anti-measles IgG titers were significantly higher in patients with severe CT involvement compared with those with non-severe involvement and remained independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement after adjustment for clinical and laboratory parameters. However, anti-measles IgG levels were not independently associated with mortality or ICU admission. Non-survivors were older, had longer hospital stays, higher CMR scores, and lower admission SpO2 levels compared with survivors. Similarly, patients requiring ICU admission had higher CMR scores and more severe thoracic CT involvement. Conclusion Higher anti-measles IgG titers were independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. These findings suggest that anti-measles IgG levels may represent a potential immunological marker associated with pulmonary disease severity rather than a direct marker of mortality risk. Further prospective studies with larger populations are needed to clarify the clinical significance of anti-measles IgG responses in COVID-19.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 具有广泛的临床谱,从轻微的呼吸道症状到严重的肺炎和死亡。先前的研究表明,在 SARS-CoV-2 感染期间,针对 麻疹 的预先存在的免疫力可能会影响 麻疹;然而,COVID-19 中抗 麻疹 IgG 滴度的临床意义仍不清楚。因此,我们的目的是调查住院 COVID-19 患者中抗 麻疹 IgG 滴度、临床严重程度、COVID-19 死亡率 率 (CMR) 评分、重症监护病房 (ICU) 要求和 死亡率 之间的关联。材料和方法 这项横断面研究包括 153 名住院的 COVID-19 患者(86 名男性和 67 名女性)。疾病严重程度根据 NIH COVID-19 治疗 指南进行分类。使用间接 ELISA 测定法测量抗 麻疹 IgG 水平。使用 COVID-19 死亡率 率 (CMR) 评分评估 死亡率 风险。结果 与病情较轻的患者相比,严重 COVID-19 和严重胸部 CT 受累的患者中观察到较高的抗 麻疹 IgG 滴度。与非严重受累患者相比,严重 CT 受累患者的抗 麻疹 IgG 滴度显着较高,并且在调整临床和实验室参数后仍与严重胸部 CT 受累独立相关。然而,抗 麻疹 IgG 水平与 死亡率 或 ICU 入住并不独立相关。与幸存者相比,非幸存者年龄更大、住院时间更长、CMR 评分更高、入院 SpO2 水平更低。同样,需要入住 ICU 的患者具有较高的 CMR 评分和更严重的胸部 CT 受累。结论 较高的抗 麻疹 IgG 滴度与住院 COVID-19 患者严重胸部 CT 受累独立相关。这些发现表明,抗 麻疹 IgG 水平可能代表与肺部疾病严重程度相关的潜在免疫标志物,而不是 死亡率 风险的直接标志物。需要对更多人群进行进一步的前瞻性研究,以阐明抗 麻疹 IgG 反应在 COVID-19 中的临床意义。

papers.title: Clinical and epidemiological profile of suspected and laboratory-confirmed measles cases in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2023
papers.abstract: Measles remains a major public health challenge in many low-resource settings, despite repeated vaccination efforts. In 2023, a resurgence of suspected measles cases was reported in South Kivu Province (Democratic Republic of Congo) following a mass vaccination campaign targeting children aged 6–59 months. This study aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of suspected measles cases and to identify factors associated with measles IgM positivity in the post-campaign period. A cross-sectional study was conducted among children aged 6–59 months presenting with clinical signs of measles in five health zones most affected by the outbreak (Kalehe, Minova, Idjwi, Miti-Murhesa, and Kalonge). Suspected cases were enrolled exhaustively from line lists provided by local health authorities. After obtaining parental consent, blood samples were collected and tested for measles and rubella IgM antibodies at the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB). Data were analyzed using R version 4.3.3. Logistic regression was used to identify characteristics associated with measles IgM positivity among suspected cases. Of the 82 children tested, 39 (48%) were positive for measles IgM. Among the 43 IgM-negative children, 8 (18%) were rubella IgM positive. In adjusted analyses, measles IgM positivity showed an evidence of an association with male parental decision-making regarding child vaccination (aOR :7.22; 95% CI: 1.64–43.2; p = 0.015) and others workers (aOR: 8.28; 95%CI:1.19-48; p = < 0.008). Despite reported high administrative vaccination coverage, measles continues to circulate among children in South Kivu. Strengthening immunization service quality, improving outreach to unvaccinated children, and engaging male parents and others workers may enhance vaccine acceptance and reduce measles transmission in the post-campaign period.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管开展了 麻疹 活动,但 麻疹 仍继续在资源匮乏的环境中构成公共卫生负担,从而给活动后 传播 动态和感染决定因素带来不确定性。该研究解决了刚果民主共和国南基伍省疑似 麻疹 病例的临床和流行病学概况以及与实验室确认相关因素的知识差距。

The study addressed a knowledge gap on the clinical and epidemiological profile of suspected measles cases and factors associated with laboratory confirmation in South Kivu Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in five health zones of South Kivu Province (Kalehe, Minova, Idjwi, Miti-Murhesa, and Kalonge) among children aged 6–59 months presenting with clinical signs of measles. analysis_en.methods: Blood samples were collected after obtaining parental consent and tested for measles and rubella IgM antibodies at the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB). Data were analyzed using R version 4.3.3, and logistic regression was used to identify characteristics associated with measles IgM positivity among suspected cases.
analysis_en.main_results: Of the 82 children tested, 39 (48%) were positive for measles IgM. Among the 43 IgM-negative children, 8 (18%) were rubella IgM positive. analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating ongoing measles circulation despite high administrative vaccination coverage, highlighting the role of parental and community decision-making in vaccine acceptance. analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening immunization service quality, improving outreach to unvaccinated children, and engaging male parents and other community workers may enhance vaccine acceptance and reduce measles transmission in the post-campaign period.

papers.title_zh: 2023 年刚果民主共和国南基伍省疑似和实验室确诊 麻疹 病例的临床和流行病学概况
papers.source_body_en: Measles remains a major public health challenge in many low-resource settings, despite repeated vaccination efforts. In 2023, a resurgence of suspected measles cases was reported in South Kivu Province (Democratic Republic of Congo) following a mass vaccination campaign targeting children aged 6–59 months. This study aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of suspected measles cases and to identify factors associated with measles IgM positivity in the post-campaign period. A cross-sectional study was conducted among children aged 6–59 months presenting with clinical signs of measles in five health zones most affected by the outbreak (Kalehe, Minova, Idjwi, Miti-Murhesa, and Kalonge). Suspected cases were enrolled exhaustively from line lists provided by local health authorities. After obtaining parental consent, blood samples were collected and tested for measles and rubella IgM antibodies at the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB). Data were analyzed using R version 4.3.3. Logistic regression was used to identify characteristics associated with measles IgM positivity among suspected cases. Of the 82 children tested, 39 (48%) were positive for measles IgM. Among the 43 IgM-negative children, 8 (18%) were rubella IgM positive. In adjusted analyses, measles IgM positivity showed an evidence of an association with male parental decision-making regarding child vaccination (aOR :7.22; 95% CI: 1.64–43.2; p = 0.015) and others workers (aOR: 8.28; 95%CI:1.19-48; p = < 0.008). Despite reported high administrative vaccination coverage, measles continues to circulate among children in South Kivu. Strengthening immunization service quality, improving outreach to unvaccinated children, and engaging male parents and others workers may enhance vaccine acceptance and reduce measles transmission in the post-campaign period.

papers.title: Universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy: a cost-effectiveness analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Measles is a highly contagious illness capable of causing significant morbidity and mortality, including adverse pregnancy outcomes. Routine screening for measles immunity is not currently recommended during pregnancy. Given the increasing frequency of measles outbreaks nationally and globally, awareness of measles immunity status can influence management of pregnant individuals who incur measles exposures, and offer an opportunity for postpartum or preconception vaccination. OBJECTIVES: We sought to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy in the United States. STUDY DESIGN: A decision-analytic model was constructed to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy compared to usual care (ie, no screening for measles immunity). The outcome of the decision analysis was quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) of the pregnant person. Model inputs were derived from the literature. Our model ran over two pregnancy cycles with a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000 per QALY. Total costs and QALYs were used to measure the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of universal measles screening compared with usual care. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the results. RESULTS: Universal screening for measles immunity was the dominant strategy. Using a measles exposure rate of 0.1% to reflect the highest risk areas, the ICER of universal screening versus no screening was $166.46/QALY. Tornado sensitivity analyses demonstrated that the cost of measles screening and the probability of measles exposure had greatest impact on the cost-effectiveness of the screening strategy. When varying the measles exposure rate from 0.001-0.1%, screening remained the dominant strategy. During Monte Carlo simulation, measles screening for immunity during pregnancy was cost-saving and increased QALYs in 99.83% of simulations. CONCLUSIONS: Universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy is a cost-effective strategy. We argue for adoption of universal measles screening during pregnancy in the United States. Until adopted, providers should consider screening their pregnant patients and recommending postpartum vaccination. If implemented, further study will be needed to assess the actual benefit of universal screening.
papers.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM

papers.title_zh: 怀孕期间 麻疹 免疫力的普遍筛查:成本效益分析。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Measles is a highly contagious illness capable of causing significant morbidity and mortality, including adverse pregnancy outcomes. Routine screening for measles immunity is not currently recommended during pregnancy. Given the increasing frequency of measles outbreaks nationally and globally, awareness of measles immunity status can influence management of pregnant individuals who incur measles exposures, and offer an opportunity for postpartum or preconception vaccination. OBJECTIVES: We sought to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy in the United States. STUDY DESIGN: A decision-analytic model was constructed to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy compared to usual care (ie, no screening for measles immunity). The outcome of the decision analysis was quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) of the pregnant person. Model inputs were derived from the literature. Our model ran over two pregnancy cycles with a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000 per QALY. Total costs and QALYs were used to measure the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of universal measles screening compared with usual care. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the results. RESULTS: Universal screening for measles immunity was the dominant strategy. Using a measles exposure rate of 0.1% to reflect the highest risk areas, the ICER of universal screening versus no screening was $166.46/QALY. Tornado sensitivity analyses demonstrated that the cost of measles screening and the probability of measles exposure had greatest impact on the cost-effectiveness of the screening strategy. When varying the measles exposure rate from 0.001-0.1%, screening remained the dominant strategy. During Monte Carlo simulation, measles screening for immunity during pregnancy was cost-saving and increased QALYs in 99.83% of simulations. CONCLUSIONS: Universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy is a cost-effective strategy. We argue for adoption of universal measles screening during pregnancy in the United States. Until adopted, providers should consider screening their pregnant patients and recommending postpartum vaccination. If implemented, further study will be needed to assess the actual benefit of universal screening.

papers.title: Characterizing Measles IgG-related Seroprevalence in the US Veteran Population during the 2025 West Texas outbreak.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2025 United States (US) measles outbreak supports concerns that measles may have significant resurgences. The study's objectives were to characterize measles serologic testing rates, estimate measles IgG seronegativity rates, and determine independent variables associated with seronegativity across the US Veterans Health Administration (VHA). METHODS: A nationwide retrospective, observational study was conducted collecting data from veterans with measles IgG antibody testing performed from January through June in 2024 (pre-outbreak) and 2025 (outbreak). Endpoints included determining independent variables associated with 1) measles IgG testing within the outbreak period versus the pre-outbreak period, and 2) measles IgG seronegativity within the outbreak period. RESULTS: 16,446 veterans had measles IgG testing in the outbreak period, a 60.3% increase in the testing rate compared to the non-outbreak period. Seronegativity was found in 1,220 (11.9%) veterans in the non-outbreak period and 1,509 veterans (9.18%) in the outbreak period (p<0.0001). Independent variables associated with seronegativity included age 64 years or below (OR 5.65, 95% CI 4.59-6.94), Janus kinase inhibitor use (OR 3.54, CI 1.24-10.1), and immunodeficient condition (OR 3.10, CI 2.34-4.11). CONCLUSIONS: As measles reemerges, certain populations were identified that may be at higher risk of infection and transmission, particularly those with immune compromise.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles resurgence in the US raised concerns about population immunity gaps. The study addressed knowledge gaps on measles IgG seronegativity rates and testing patterns in the US veteran population during the 2025 outbreak.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide retrospective observational study was conducted using the US Veterans Health Administration (VHA) database. Veterans with measles IgG antibody testing performed from January through June in 2024 (pre-outbreak) and 2025 (outbreak) were included.
analysis.methods: Data were collected on measles IgG testing and serostatus during pre-outbreak and outbreak periods. Independent variables associated with seronegativity were determined using statistical models.
analysis.main_results: Measles IgG testing increased by 60.3% during the outbreak period (16,446 veterans tested). Seronegativity was 11.9% in the non-outbreak period and 9.18% in the outbreak period (p<0.0001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as identifying populations at higher risk of infection and transmission, particularly those with immune compromise. They highlighted the need for targeted interventions in these groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform vaccination strategies and targeted serologic screening in veterans, especially those with immunodeficiency or on Janus kinase inhibitors, to mitigate measles resurgence risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's retrospective design and reliance on existing VHA data may limit generalizability and introduce selection bias. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This nationwide retrospective study assessed measles IgG seroprevalence in the US veteran population during the 2025 outbreak. Testing rates rose by 60.3% compared to the pre-outbreak period, with seronegativity decreasing from 11.9% to 9.18%. Independent risk factors for seronegativity included age ≤64 years, Janus kinase inhibitor use, and immunodeficient conditions. The authors conclude that targeted interventions are needed for high-risk groups to address measles resurgence. Limitations include retrospective design and potential selection bias, warranting cautious interpretation.

RESULTS: 16,446 veterans had measles IgG testing in the outbreak period, a 60.3% increase in the testing rate compared to the non-outbreak period. Seronegativity was found in 1,220 (11.9%) veterans in the non-outbreak period and 1,509 veterans (9.18%) in the outbreak period (p<0.0001). Independent variables associated with seronegativity included age 64 years or below (OR 5.65, 95% CI 4.59-6.94), Janus kinase inhibitor use (OR 3.54, CI 1.24-10.1), and immunodeficient condition (OR 3.10, CI 2.34-4.11). CONCLUSIONS: As measles reemerges, certain populations were identified that may be at higher risk of infection and transmission, particularly those with immune compromise.

analysis_zh.main_results: 麻疹 IgG 检测在 麻疹 期间增加了 60.3%(检测了 16,446 名退伍军人)。非 暴发 期间的血清阴性率为 11.9%,暴发 期间的血清阴性率为 9.18%(p<0.0001)。

papers.title: Measles in Poland in 2024
papers.abstract: Background Measles remains one of the most contagious viral diseases, and its elimination in the WHO European Region requires maintaining high vaccination rates and effective epidemiological surveillance. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, many European countries, including Poland, are seeing a renewed increase in the number of cases. Objective The aim of the study was to assess the epidemiological situation of measles in Poland in 2024, taking into account the vaccination status of the population against measles and the degree of implementation of the World Health Organization (WHO) measles eradication program in Poland. Material and methods The epidemiological situation of measles in Poland in 2024 was assessed using data obtained from the national infectious disease surveillance system, recorded by the local sanitary and epidemiological stations in the Epibaza system. Additional information was obtained from the annual bulletins “Infectious Diseases and Poisonings in Poland” and “Vaccinations in Poland” for the years 2015-2024. Results In 2024, an increase in the number of measles cases was recorded in Poland. A total of 272 cases were reported (incidence rate 0.72/100,000), compared with 35 cases in 2023 (0.09/100,000), representing representing more than a sevenfold increase, largely due to the very low number of cases in the previous year. The rise in reported cases was associated with several measles outbreaks, primarily in the Mazowieckie and Dolnośląskie voivodeships. Altogether, 23 outbreaks were identified. Analysis in relation to the pre-COVID-19 period (2019) indicates a persistently lower incidence rate. In 2019, 1,502 cases were reported (3.31/100,000). Compared with the median for 2018-2022, the number of cases in 2024 was more than eight times higher. The highest incidence was observed among children aged 0-9 years. The increase in cases and hospitalizations coincided with a decline in vaccination coverage below 95%, increasing the risk of local outbreaks. Conclusions Maintaining measles elimination in Poland requires sustaining at least 95% coverage with two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine. This should be supported by continued routine immunization, catch-up vaccination of susceptible individuals, and further strengthening of epidemiological and laboratory surveillance, including molecular characterization of circulating measles viruses.

papers.title: Discrete state-structured epidemic model with varying susceptibility and infectivity and its application to the measles outbreak in the United States
papers.abstract: Host individuals with vaccinations for infectious diseases often transition among different states of susceptibility and infectivity. Thus, we derive a class of epidemic models in which susceptible and infected individuals have a discrete set of susceptibility and infectivity states, respectively. Our model is based on double-dose vaccination and accounts for all possible state transitions between states. A comprehensive mathematical analysis of the proposed model is conducted, including assessing the control reproduction number and the global dynamical behaviors of the solutions. By using an improved affine-invariant ensemble Markov chain Monte Carlo method, we also fit the model with measles case data in the United States. The results indicate that despite high vaccination coverage and efficacy rates, sporadic or small-scale measles outbreaks still occur. This suggests that reliance solely on vaccination policies is insufficient to fully interrupt its transmission chain. Consequently, enhancing the diagnosis rate of measles cases is another crucial measure for controlling measles transmission and outbreaks, building upon existing vaccination efforts.

papers.title: Quantifying the impact of time-delayed reporting and supportive care in measles outbreak: A simulation approach for Texas, USA.
papers.abstract: This study examines how time delays in vaccination response, case reporting, and access to supportive care influence measles transmission during the recent outbreak in Texas, USA. We develop a delay-based compartmental model that captures both biological and operational features of measles control and calibrate it using Texas reported Measles incidence data from January 20 to May 27, 2025. Analytical and numerical results show that delays in reporting and intervention can substantially weaken outbreak control, allowing transmission to persist even in highly vaccinated populations. In contrast, timely case detection, improved vaccination uptake, and access to supportive care significantly reduce transmission and can drive the effective reproduction number below unity. These findings highlight the critical role of minimizing reporting and healthcare delays alongside sustained immunization efforts to prevent measles resurgence and support elimination goals in Texas and similar settings.

papers.source_body_en: This study examines how time delays in vaccination response, case reporting, and access to supportive care influence measles transmission during the recent outbreak in Texas, USA. We develop a delay-based compartmental model that captures both biological and operational features of measles control and calibrate it using Texas reported Measles incidence data from January 20 to May 27, 2025. Analytical and numerical results show that delays in reporting and intervention can substantially weaken outbreak control, allowing transmission to persist even in highly vaccinated populations. In contrast, timely case detection, improved vaccination uptake, and access to supportive care significantly reduce transmission and can drive the effective reproduction number below unity. These findings highlight the critical role of minimizing reporting and healthcare delays alongside sustained immunization efforts to prevent measles resurgence and support elimination goals in Texas and similar settings.
papers.abstract_zh: 本研究探讨了最近在美国德克萨斯州发生的 麻疹 期间,疫苗接种 反应、病例报告和获得支持性护理的时间延迟如何影响 麻疹 传播。我们开发了一种基于延迟的区室模型,该模型捕获了 麻疹 控制的生物学和操作特征,并使用德克萨斯州报告的 2025 年 1 月 20 日至 5 月 27 日的 麻疹 发病率 数据对其进行校准。分析和数值结果表明,报告和干预的延迟会大大削弱 麻疹 控制,使 传播 即使在高度接种疫苗的情况下也能持续存在人口。相比之下,及时发现病例、提高 疫苗接种 的吸收率以及获得支持性护理可显着减少 传播 的数量,并可使有效繁殖数低于统一值。这些发现强调了最大限度地减少报告和医疗延误以及持续免疫工作对于防止 麻疹 卷土重来并支持德克萨斯州和类似地区消除 麻疹 目标的关键作用。

papers.title: Infection with measles virus induces leukopenia and rash in a humanized immune system mouse model
papers.abstract: Abstract Humans are the natural hosts of the measles virus (MV). With the exception of non-human primates, no other animal species are naturally susceptible to MV infection. Thus, no small animal models exist to study the mechanisms of MV pathogenicity. The aim of the present study was to establish a small animal model of MV infection using NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) immunodeficient mice implanted with human-cord-blood-derived CD34 + cells and to evaluate its suitability as a measles model. Upon infecting the humanized mice with a recombinant wild-type strain MV expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), a strong EGFP signal was detected in the spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow. This fluorescence was confirmed to be associated with MV infection in human T and B cells. Furthermore, the mice exhibited leukopenia and rash-like green fluorescent foci reminiscent of a measles rash. These foci originated from the accumulation of human leukocytes adjacent to hair follicles, consistent with the pathology observed in non-human primate models. These results suggest that this small animal model could be a valuable tool for elucidating the mechanisms of MV infection and its pathogenicity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles virus (MV) is a human pathogen with no naturally susceptible small animal model, limiting mechanistic studies of its pathogenicity. The study addressed the lack of suitable animal models by asking whether a humanized immune system mouse could recapitulate MV infection and disease features.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study established a small animal model using NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) immunodeficient mice implanted with human-cord-blood-derived CD34+ cells to evaluate MV infection. The aim was to assess the suitability of this model for studying MV pathogenicity.
analysis.methods: The authors infected humanized mice with a recombinant wild-type measles virus strain expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) and evaluated infection through fluorescence detection in tissues and assessment of clinical signs.
analysis.main_results: Upon infection, strong EGFP signals were detected in the spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow, confirmed to be associated with MV infection in human T and B cells. The mice exhibited leukopenia and rash-like green fluorescent foci consistent with measles pathology.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the humanized mouse model recapitulates key features of MV infection and pathogenicity observed in non-human primates. They concluded that this model provides a valuable tool for elucidating MV mechanisms.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This model may enable mechanistic studies of MV pathogenesis, drug testing, and vaccine evaluation that were previously infeasible due to the lack of small animal models. It could also facilitate research into measles-associated complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to an abstract-only report, which restricts detailed methodological and result reporting. The strength of the evidence is low due to the absence of full methodological descriptions, sample sizes, statistical analyses, and comprehensive pathological assessments.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the lack of small animal models for measles virus (MV) by developing a humanized mouse model using NSG mice engrafted with human CD34+ cells. Upon infection with a recombinant MV expressing EGFP, the mice showed viral infection in human T and B cells in lymphoid tissues and developed leukopenia and rash-like lesions. The authors concluded that this model recapitulates key features of MV infection and pathogenicity seen in non-human primates, offering a potential tool for mechanistic studies. However, the evidence is limited to an abstract, providing no details on sample sizes, statistical methods, or comprehensive pathology, which constrains the strength of the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 麻疹病毒 (MV) 是一种人类病原体,没有天然易感的小动物模型,限制了其致病性的机制研究。该研究通过询问人源化免疫系统小鼠是否可以重现 MV 感染和疾病特征,解决了缺乏合适动物模型的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用植入人脐带血来源的 CD34+ 细胞的 NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) 免疫缺陷小鼠建立了小动物模型来评估 MV 感染。目的是评估该模型对于研究 MV 致病性的适用性。
elements_zh.methods: 作者用表达增强型绿色荧光蛋白 (EGFP) 的重组野生型 麻疹病毒 菌株感染人源化小鼠,并通过组织中的荧光检测和临床症状评估来评估感染情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 感染后,在脾脏、淋巴结和骨髓中检测到强 EGFP 信号,证实与人类 T 和 B 细胞中的 MV 感染有关。小鼠表现出白细胞减少症和皮疹样绿色荧光病灶,与 麻疹 病理学一致。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Measles virus (MV) is a human pathogen with no naturally susceptible small animal model, limiting mechanistic studies of its pathogenicity. analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study established a small animal model using NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) immunodeficient mice implanted with human-cord-blood-derived CD34+ cells to evaluate MV infection. analysis_en.methods: The authors infected humanized mice with a recombinant wild-type measles virus strain expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) and evaluated infection through fluorescence detection in tissues and assessment of clinical signs.

papers.title_zh: 麻疹病毒 感染会在人源化免疫系统小鼠模型中诱发白细胞减少症和皮疹
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Humans are the natural hosts of the measles virus (MV). With the exception of non-human primates, no other animal species are naturally susceptible to MV infection. Thus, no small animal models exist to study the mechanisms of MV pathogenicity. The aim of the present study was to establish a small animal model of MV infection using NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) immunodeficient mice implanted with human-cord-blood-derived CD34 + cells and to evaluate its suitability as a measles model. Upon infecting the humanized mice with a recombinant wild-type strain MV expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), a strong EGFP signal was detected in the spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow. This fluorescence was confirmed to be associated with MV infection in human T and B cells. Furthermore, the mice exhibited leukopenia and rash-like green fluorescent foci reminiscent of a measles rash. These foci originated from the accumulation of human leukocytes adjacent to hair follicles, consistent with the pathology observed in non-human primate models. These results suggest that this small animal model could be a valuable tool for elucidating the mechanisms of MV infection and its pathogenicity.

papers.title: The 2026 Measles Outbreak in Bangladesh: A Critique of Immunity Gaps and Care Deficiencies
papers.abstract: Bangladesh entered 2026 amid a severe measles outbreak that peaked in mid-May. This article analyses the public health response to the outbreak and evaluates the government's management of the crisis. Health professionals and measles experts have attributed the outbreak to accumulated gaps in routine immunisation, weaknesses in public health infrastructure, poor nutritional status among children, widespread vitamin A deficiency, and maternal undernutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

papers.title: Barriers to disease notification among primary healthcare physicians in West Bank, Palestine: a cross-sectional survey
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Underreporting remains a persistent challenge for infectious disease surveillance systems. Evidence on notification knowledge and practices among physicians in the West Bank remains limited, although they play a critical role in disease notification. We aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of primary healthcare physicians in disease notification, identify factors associated with appropriate notification of suspected mumps, measles, and chickenpox cases, and describe barriers to notification. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional survey on primary healthcare physicians in the Palestinian Ministry of Health primary healthcare centers between August 2024 and May 2025. The questionnaire assessed knowledge, attitudes, and self-reported notification practices. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with recent notification practices. Results Among 223 respondents, 30.9% were categorized as having a good knowledge score of the disease notification process across multiple operational domains of disease notification, while 93.3% were categorized as having a good attitude score. Common misconceptions included laboratory confirmation being required for notification (61.0%) and that surveillance case definitions require laboratory criteria (65.5%). Over 80% of respondents notified their last-encountered measles, mumps, or chickenpox case. However, timely notification was lower; 52.4% of measles cases were reported immediately, compared with 19.3% of mumps and 14.0% of chickenpox cases reported within the recommended timeframes. Commonly reported barriers included lack of time (60.5%), and uncertainty about which diseases to notify (38.1%) and when (32.3%). Knowledge and attitude scores were not significantly associated with notification practices, although limited observations and composite scores may have obscured these associations. Physicians who received recent supervisory feedback on disease notification had higher odds of notifying chickenpox cases (OR: 4.01, 95%CI: 1.40-11.43). Compared to general practitioners, other medical specialties had lower odds of notifying mumps (OR: 0.21, 95%CI: 0.06–0.81) and chickenpox cases (OR: 0.23, 95%CI: 0.08–0.69). Conclusions Despite positive attitudes towards the notification system, knowledge gaps and misconceptions may contribute to underreporting of notifiable conditions. Strengthening training, clarifying guidance, improving feedback mechanisms, and addressing identified barriers and preferences may enhance disease notification performance by primary healthcare physicians in the West Bank.

papers.title: ECHO: A lightweight tool for inferring missing case counts from pathogen phylogenies
papers.abstract: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOWTimed phylogenetic trees express the evolutionary history of a pathogen outbreak in units of time, providing an estimate of the elapsed time across the shared ancestry of a set of taxa. By combining this elapsed time with known information about the epidemiology of a disease, we can relate the total branch length to the total number of cases related to the phylogeny. This gives information about the number of unsequenced cases that are related to the phylogeny. We call these "cryptic" cases. We present ECHO (Estimation of Cryptic Hosts from Outbreak trees), a collection of three lightweight estimators of the number of cryptic cases in a phylogeny. ECHO is agnostic to the form of the sampling process, making it robust to a variety of forms of sampling heterogeneity. We demonstrate ECHOs baseline accuracy and its robustness to heterogenous sampling frameworks through simulation. Additionally, we apply ECHO to measles virus sequences that were collected during an outbreak in the USA in 2021. ECHO is able to recover the number of cryptic cases with a reasonable degree of accuracy both in simulation and in practice. We discuss the contexts in which ECHO is most applicable, and the interpretation of its estimates.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Phylogenetic trees of pathogens provide evolutionary time scales but do not directly quantify unsequenced cases linked to an outbreak. The study addresses the knowledge gap in estimating the number of cryptic cases that are epidemiologically connected to sequenced samples but not represented in the phylogeny.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study introduces ECHO (Estimation of Cryptic Hosts from Outbreak trees), a tool comprising three lightweight estimators designed to infer missing case counts from timed phylogenetic trees. The authors demonstrate the tool’s performance through simulation and apply it to measles virus sequences collected during a 2021 outbreak in the USA.
analysis.methods: ECHO uses timed phylogenetic trees to relate total branch length to the total number of cases, thereby estimating cryptic cases. The tool is designed to be agnostic to sampling processes, ensuring robustness to heterogeneous sampling frameworks. Simulation studies and application to real-world measles virus data were used to evaluate accuracy.
analysis.main_results: ECHO recovered the number of cryptic cases with a reasonable degree of accuracy both in simulation and in practice when applied to measles virus sequences from the 2021 USA outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret ECHO’s estimates as providing actionable insights into the extent of cryptic transmission during outbreaks. The novelty lies in the development of a lightweight, sampling-agnostic tool specifically designed to infer missing case counts from phylogenetic data.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: ECHO can inform outbreak investigation and response by quantifying cryptic cases, thereby improving surveillance accuracy and guiding public health interventions for measles and potentially other pathogens with similar transmission dynamics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report the specific sample sizes, statistical confidence intervals, or detailed limitations beyond the tool’s agnosticism to sampling heterogeneity. The evidence strength is moderate, as the findings are supported by simulation and a single real-world application.

analysis.summary_en: ECHO is a lightweight tool designed to estimate the number of cryptic cases linked to a pathogen outbreak using timed phylogenetic trees. The study addresses the gap in quantifying unsequenced cases by relating phylogenetic branch length to total case counts. ECHO comprises three estimators and is robust to heterogeneous sampling frameworks. The tool was validated through simulation and applied to measles virus sequences from a 2021 USA outbreak, demonstrating reasonable accuracy in recovering cryptic case counts. The authors interpret the estimates as providing actionable insights into cryptic transmission. ECHO has potential public health significance by improving surveillance accuracy and guiding interventions for measles and similar pathogens.

papers.title_zh: ECHO:一种轻量级工具,用于根据病原体系统发育推断缺失病例数
papers.source_body_en: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOWTimed phylogenetic trees express the evolutionary history of a pathogen outbreak in units of time, providing an estimate of the elapsed time across the shared ancestry of a set of taxa. By combining this elapsed time with known information about the epidemiology of a disease, we can relate the total branch length to the total number of cases related to the phylogeny. This gives information about the number of unsequenced cases that are related to the phylogeny. We call these "cryptic" cases. We present ECHO (Estimation of Cryptic Hosts from Outbreak trees), a collection of three lightweight estimators of the number of cryptic cases in a phylogeny. ECHO is agnostic to the form of the sampling process, making it robust to a variety of forms of sampling heterogeneity. We demonstrate ECHOs baseline accuracy and its robustness to heterogenous sampling frameworks through simulation. Additionally, we apply ECHO to measles virus sequences that were collected during an outbreak in the USA in 2021. ECHO is able to recover the number of cryptic cases with a reasonable degree of accuracy both in simulation and in practice. We discuss the contexts in which ECHO is most applicable, and the interpretation of its estimates.
papers.abstract_zh: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOW定时系统发育树以时间单位表达病原体 暴发 的进化历史,提供对一组类群的共同祖先的经过时间的估计。通过将经过的时间与有关疾病 流行病学 的已知信息相结合,我们可以将总分支长度与与 系统发育 相关的病例总数联系起来。这提供了与 系统发育 相关的未排序案例数量的信息。我们称这些为“神秘”案例。我们提出了 ECHO(Estimation of Cryptic 宿主 from 暴发 trees),它是 系统发育 中神秘案例数量的三个轻量级估计器的集合。ECHO 与采样过程的形式无关,这使其对各种形式的采样异质性具有鲁棒性。我们通过模拟展示了 ECHO 的基线准确性及其对异构采样框架的鲁棒性。此外,我们将 ECHO 应用于 2021 年在美国 麻疹病毒 期间收集的 麻疹病毒 序列。ECHO 能够在模拟和实践中以合理的准确度恢复神秘病例的数量。我们讨论 ECHO 最适用的环境及其估计的解释。

papers.title: Strengthening Outbreak Response and Preparedness in US Health Departments Through a Community of Practice.
papers.abstract: The reemergence of infectious diseases, such as measles, in the United States has placed significant strain on state, local, tribal, and territorial health departments to respond and contain the spread of disease. The actions by health departments have spanned a wide range of outbreak preparedness and response initiatives, with some health departments excelling in their approaches while others work to build capacity despite resource constraints. To strengthen outbreak preparedness and response, the Johns Hopkins Center for Outbreak Response Innovation convened a national Community of Practice series in 2025, bringing together 115 participants from 40 health departments. Presentations emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration, system adaptability, and continuous learning to enhance outbreak response capacity. This series underscored that sustainable improvements in public health practice rely on bridging academic research and operational realities through shared learning networks, ensuring that technical innovations translate into effective and scalable disease response strategies nationwide.
papers.journal: Journal of public health management and practice : JPHMP

papers.title: Routine early childhood vaccination uptake before and during the COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland: A population-based cohort study of administrative data.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The COVID-19 pandemic changed the working patterns of many families and led to an increased focus on vaccines. This may have influenced early childhood vaccination uptake. We utilised linked administrative health data for Scotland to investigate whether the pandemic was associated with changes in uptake of early childhood vaccinations. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort design examining population-based individual-level linked administrative health data for Scotland. METHODS: We assessed timely uptake of six routine vaccinations - 6-in-1 vaccine, pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV), rotavirus vaccine, Hib/MenC vaccine, measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine and PCV booster - among children reaching 12 months or 24 months of age in Scotland, January 2019-December 2021 (N = 199,574 children). Logistic regression modelling assessed uptake among a pandemic cohort compared to a pre-pandemic cohort, with and without adjustment for key sociodemographic variables. Interaction analysis assessed whether associations varied across area deprivation, parental socioeconomic class, urban-rural residence, and maternal ethnic group. RESULTS: Vaccination uptake either remained stable or increased for five of the six vaccines during the pandemic. Most interactions were not statistically significant, indicating broadly similar pandemic effects across sociodemographic groups. However, large pre-existing inequalities remained during the pandemic, with least-deprived areas and managerial/professional households having higher uptake, and several minority ethnic groups having lower uptake. CONCLUSIONS: Scotland's childhood immunisation programme showed resilience during the pandemic, but pre-existing inequalities persisted. Future planning should include safeguarding early-life vaccines and addressing structural barriers.
